questions.prompt: ¿Qué quiere Sofía en la primera historia?
questions.explanation: You understood a whole story with just three new structures: hay, quiere, tiene. TPRS limits new language on purpose, so everything you hear stays comprehensible.
We asked yes/no and either/or questions about the same sentences again and again. That is "circling": many meaningful repetitions without boring drills.
Words from stories 1 and 2 came back in story 3. Meeting them again in a new context is what moves them into long-term memory.

questions.prompt: Why are the stories a little absurd (a cat with ideas, a dog that steals pizza)?
options: Because surprising stories are easier to remember
Because Spanish speakers talk like that
questions.correct: Because surprising stories are easier to remember
questions.explanation: Emotion and surprise make language memorable. In live classes, students even help create the story.

questions.prompt: What did you NOT need to do in this course?
questions.explanation: You acquire a language by understanding messages, not by studying rules. Grammar comes naturally once you have heard it many times.
